records.name: Goyim Defense League (GDL)
records.targets: Jewish people; also promotes racist and anti-LGBTQ+ narratives
records.membership: ADL describes a few dozen core influencers/live streamers, a larger supporter base for physical activity, and tens of thousands of online followers; these are not equivalent measures of active membership.
records.armed_status: Not a conventional armed organization; public reporting focuses on propaganda, harassment, demonstrations and some criminal cases.
records.notes: Good example of separating core members, supporters, viewers and affiliates rather than using one membership number.

records.name: National Justice Party (NJP)
records.status: dissolved late 2023; successor activity through splinter NOVA
records.targets: Jews, immigrants and racial minorities within its white-supremacist ideology
records.membership: No reliable current membership because NJP dissolved; former members may appear in successor networks.
records.armed_status: Not best classified as an armed group; assess violence claims individually.
records.notes: The successor edge is more informative than keeping a dissolved organization marked simply 'active'.

records.name: New England White Network (NEWN)
records.status: small active/observed network in recent reporting
geography: New Hampshire and New England, United States
records.targets: Racial minorities, immigrants and other groups targeted by white-supremacist ideology
records.armed_status: No basis for classifying the network as an armed organization.
records.notes: Useful small-network node for regional propagation analysis.

records.name: Asatru Folk Assembly (AFA)
records.targets: Promotes white-identity religious nationalism and exclusionary racial ideology; assess claims by source and period.
records.membership: No reliable public current membership census.
records.notes: Important for separating religious identity, ethnonationalism and hate-group classification.

records.name: Aryan Freedom Network (AFN)
records.targets: Racial and religious minorities according to white-supremacist ideology
records.armed_status: No basis for treating the organization as a conventional armed force.
records.notes: Keep exact organizational identity separate from similarly named groups.

records.name: Rise Above Movement (R.A.M.)
records.status: historically active; network influence persists through successor/Active Club ecosystem
records.targets: Jews, immigrants, racial minorities and political opponents within white-supremacist ideology
records.membership: Small movement; no reliable current census.
records.armed_status: Militant street movement; not a conventional armed organization.
records.notes: Useful predecessor node for the Active Club graph.

records.name: Nationalist Social Club (NSC-131)
records.targets: Black people, Jews, immigrants, LGBTQ+ people and other groups targeted by neo-Nazi ideology
records.membership: No reliable public census; public activity is usually measured through demonstrations and propaganda.
records.armed_status: Not a conventional armed organization; individual conduct should be separately documented.
affiliations: Goyim Defense League overlap documented in public reporting
records.notes: Network coupling should be represented with dated collaboration edges rather than merged identities.

records.name: White Lives Matter movement
records.targets: Racial equality movements, immigrants and minority communities in its white-supremacist manifestations
records.membership: No central membership; label used by many small groups and individuals.
records.notes: Treat as a movement/label node, not a corporation-like organization.

records.name: Sovereign Citizen Movement
geography: other countries with related pseudo-legal movements
records.targets: Government institutions and officials are treated as illegitimate by adherents; some rhetoric also targets minorities or political opponents, but ideology varies.
records.membership: No reliable central count because it is a decentralized belief/movement category.
records.armed_status: Not uniformly armed; public law-enforcement and court records document some violent incidents by individual adherents.
affiliations: Some Goyim Defense League affiliates have adopted sovereign-citizen tactics
records.notes: Excellent cross-layer node between extremism, pseudo-law, fraud/harassment and individual violence.

records.name: National Socialist Black Metal (NSBM) network
records.targets: Targets vary by band; common themes include antisemitism, racial supremacy and Nazi symbolism.
records.armed_status: Not an armed organization; individual musicians or scenes must be assessed separately.
records.notes: Useful for studying cultural transmission without treating a music genre as one organization.

records.name: Twelve Tribes Communities
records.targets: Not primarily a hate-group category; controversy centers on communal authority, discipline, child-rearing and labor practices.
records.membership: Public estimates vary; no single independently verified current global count.
records.notes: Include because the user's requested dataset should distinguish high-control research from hate-group research.

records.name: Children of God / The Family International
records.targets: Not primarily a hate group; historical research focuses on communal control, sexual norms and documented abuse controversies.
records.membership: Membership changed substantially across decades; no reliable single current number.
records.notes: Separate historical allegations, court findings and survivor testimony by evidence type.

records.name: Unification movement / Family Federation for World Peace and Unification
records.status: active international movement; internal terminology and organizational structures have changed
records.targets: Not a hate-group category; research focuses on theology, authority, organizational structure, political networks and disputed 'cult' classification.
records.membership: Public estimates vary widely; no universally accepted current global figure.
affiliations: Multiple affiliated businesses, media and political organizations historically associated with the broader movement
records.notes: Do not collapse every affiliated organization into the religious body without an explicit relationship edge.

records.name: Davidian / Branch Davidian successor communities
records.membership: Small and fragmented; no unified membership count.
records.armed_status: 1993 Waco history involved armed confrontation, but successor communities must not be assumed to share that status.
records.notes: Use predecessor/successor edges to prevent historical Waco data being misapplied to unrelated communities.

records.name: Aleph (Aum Shinrikyo successor)
records.status: active successor organization under monitoring/restrictions in Japan
records.targets: Not a conventional hate-group category; historical continuity and doctrinal change from Aum are the research questions.
records.membership: Smaller than Aum at its peak; exact current numbers require dated source verification.
records.armed_status: The original Aum organization carried out chemical terrorism; successor status and current capabilities must be separately assessed.
records.notes: Never inherit Aum's 1995 capabilities automatically into a successor record.

records.name: Hikari no Wa
records.targets: Not a conventional hate-group category; research focuses on its relationship to Aum and its public distancing from Aum violence.
records.membership: Small; current estimates require dated verification.
records.armed_status: No basis in the cited high-level record for classifying it as an armed movement.
records.notes: A good test case for successor differentiation.

research_note: The expansion deliberately includes both hate/extremist organizations and contested high-control religious movements. 'Cult' is treated as a descriptive or contested term rather than a universal legal category. Every record should carry a classification confidence and source date before being promoted to a strong empirical graph claim.
